title: Edge Conductor standup brief — VPC/on-prem install pulse (2026-11-02)
summary: Quick weekly pulse capturing install progress, recurring blockers, and action items for the Edge Conductor cohort (VPC/on-prem). Focus on three customer installs and infra noise affecting KV cache warmup.
content:
Standup: Edge Conductor — weekly pulse
Date: 2026-11-02
Authors: Aisha T. (owner); notes captured live
Context: small cohort of on-prem and VPC installs in parallel. This doc is a working capture — unsanitized notes, open questions and short-term actions. Use this to brief SRE and Solutions before noon sync.

Key installs in flight
- Customer: Parkside Health (on‑prem rack)
  - Current state: rack racked, SAS storage validated; burn-in tests passed but node 3 shows occasional GPU power cycling on long sequences (>8k tokens) during compile-time stress. Happened twice overnight.
  - Impact: degraded model load times and intermittent OOM-like failures in the local compile shim. Customer has paused first-stage rollout.
  - Workaround tried: pinned model variant to quantized v1.3; restarted node 3, forced kernel fallback to CPU for compile step -> build completed, but throughput impacted.
  - Next steps: Samir to run remote BMC logs + firmware inventory; if firmware mismatch, schedule downtime with Parkside for BIOS/firmware update (ETA: 48-72h). Link: PD-7891.

- Customer: Veridian Analytics (VPC private deployment)
  - Current state: Deploy succeeded; intermittent latency spikes from 11:00–12:00 PST correlating to scheduled nightly backup outside our control (customer infra). Spikes add ~60–120ms tail latency for short-chat requests.
  - Investigation: observed KV cache eviction bursts during backup window — storage IOPS throttling causing slow checkpoint writes. We recommended adjusting cache flush interval; customer is evaluating.
  - Action: Miguel to propose parameter changes (cache_flush_ms, max_kv_items) and run A/B across a canary route. Target: reduce tail latency by 50% during window.

- Customer: Templar Financials (edge appliance)
  - Current state: install prep complete; security runbook review flagged 2 items: internal cert rotation cadence and HSM integration test missing. Customer needs SOC-2 reported doc on key custody.
  - Action: Priya to produce short HSM test script and hand-off template; Jason from security to approve. Priya estimates 2 business days.

Recurring blockers and observations
- Node provisioning fragility (node tiling and IP reuse)
  - Symptoms: when nodes reprovision quickly after failed playbook step, kubelet churn leaves stale iptables rules -> slow pod networking for ~5–10 minutes until netfilter garbage collect.
  - Temporary mitigation: add a small cooldown (30s) and an iptables cleanup hook in the provisioner. Engineering time estimate: 1 day to land; regression risk low.
  - Owner: Aisha + infra team to schedule in next sprint.

- Telemetry gap for KV cache warmup
  - Problem: we don't have a per-node metric for 'kv_cache_fill_rate' visible in Console; makes it hard to correlate customer reports of initial cold latency.
  - Proposed fix: emit a 'kv_cache_metrics' event (counts and percent filled) to tracing for first 10 min after model load. Low overhead. Samir volunteered a PR.

- On-prem DNS edge case
  - Case: Parkside had an internal DNS time-to-live misconfigured (30s) leading to our node agent refreshing service endpoints too aggressively. Caused brief reconnection storms.
  - Note: add DNS sanity checklist to preflight (min ttl >=300s), include in runbook.

Decisions made
- No immediate rollback: for Parkside, do firmware-first path; avoid model variant downgrade unless compiles continue to fail under updated firmware.
- Canary strategy for Veridian: run canary route for 48 hours with reduced cache flush frequency; if tail latency improves, recommend cluster-wide change.

Open questions
- Should we expose a 'firmware-compatibility' flag in installer output? (Pros: faster triage; Cons: more surface area to maintain). Tentatively defer — gather data from two more incidents.
- For HSM integration: are we comfortable shipping a minimal test harness in the private artifact, or should it be a customer-run script only? Security team to advise.

Action items (owners, ETA)
- Samir Das: gather BMC + firmware logs for Parkside; escalate to firmware vendor if mismatch (ETA: 2026-11-04).
- Miguel Rivera: propose cache param set and run canary A/B for Veridian (ETA: 2026-11-05).
- Priya Patel: deliver HSM test script + handoff template (ETA: 2026-11-04); coordinate with Security (Jason L.).
- Aisha Thompson + infra: add 30s cooldown + iptables cleanup hook in provisioner; land in sprint-48 (ETA: 2026-11-12).
- Samir Das: open PR to surface kv_cache metrics to tracing and Console (ETA: 2026-11-06).
- Product Ops: add DNS TTL check to preflight checklist and update runbook (owner: product-ops, ETA: 2026-11-08).

Notes-to-self / quick followups
- Prep a 1-page slide for Solutions 11/05 handoff focusing on risk: firmware + kv cache gaps.
- Revisit whether default cache_flush_ms should be lowered globally; measure impact on egress IOPS first.
- Keep Parkside on a restricted maintenance window until firmware verdict.

Meeting attendees (live sync 11:00 PST)
- Aisha Thompson (install owner)
- Samir Das (on-call infra)
- Miguel Rivera (perf eng)
- Priya Patel (solutions)
- Jason Lee (security, part-time)
- Customer points: Parkside infra lead (Lena M.) — joined for first 30m

Appendix: quick logs and snippets
- Parkside BMC note: IPMI log snippet shows 'power cycle requested' at 02:14:03 UTC; follow-up required.
- Veridian perf trace: spike at 11:11 correlates with backup job 'db-snap-01' IOPS burst.
- HSM ask: customer requires lab-run of encrypt/decrypt PKCS#11 flows; minimal script attached to shared confluence page.

End.
